title: Listening: Idioms in Conversation
description: Listen to everyday lines with common idioms and choose what each speaker really means.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

media.text: Don't worry about the math exam. Honestly, it was a piece of cake.

questions.explanation: "A piece of cake" means something very easy.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

media.text: I think I'll skip the gym today. I'm feeling a bit under the weather.

options.text: She's going to bed early tonight

questions.explanation: "Under the weather" means feeling slightly ill.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker want the listener to do?

media.text: We're planning a surprise party for Jen on Friday. Whatever you do, don't let the cat out of the bag.

questions.explanation: "Don't let the cat out of the bag" means don't reveal a secret.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

media.text: We got great seats for the concert, but they cost an arm and a leg.

questions.explanation: "Cost an arm and a leg" means cost a lot of money.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

media.text: It's almost eight and we've finished the hardest part. Let's call it a day.

questions.explanation: "Call it a day" means to stop working, usually because you've done enough.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

media.text: The repairman cut corners on our roof, and now it's leaking again.

options.text: He did the job quickly and carelessly
He refused to do the job

questions.explanation: "Cut corners" means doing something the cheapest or easiest way, often skipping important steps.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

media.text: What if it rains on the day of the picnic? Well, we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.

options.text: She will decide later after she has more information
She wants to build a bridge

questions.explanation: "Cross that bridge when we come to it" means deal with a problem only when it happens.

questions.prompt: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

media.text: Mark said the real problem is poor communication, and I think he hit the nail on the head.

options.text: Mark is very busy at work
Mark said exactly the right thing

questions.explanation: "Hit the nail on the head" means to describe something exactly right.
